B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
A: Yeah, hello. I can hear you. I'm Tomasz.
B: Gemma. Nice to meet you. How was your first one?
A: Was good, yeah. Nice lady. We talked about kids mostly, and football on Saturday.
B: Ah, that's nice. Mine was a bird man, so I got a lot of bats and owls. I enjoyed it, actually. So what do you do, Tomasz?
A: I fit kitchens. Carpenter. Small company in Basingstoke.
B: Oh, no way! I'm an upholsterer, so I'm sort of on the edge of your world. I do a bit of woodwork as well, but just repairs, you know, re-gluing chair frames, that kind of thing.
A: Ah, okay. Chairs, yeah. Old chairs, the joints go loose.
B: Exactly that! Everyone's grandad has had a go with a few nails and some glue, and then I have to get it all out. What's the worst thing you find, when you take a kitchen out?
A: Er... mostly water. Under the sink, everything rotten, and the customer says, oh, we didn't know. For ten years they didn't know. And sometimes the walls are not straight at all, so you scribe the worktop, take your time. When it fits nice to the wall, no gap, that's best part of job, to be honest.
B: Oh, I love that. That's like when the pattern lines up across the seat and the back. Nobody notices it, but you notice it.
A: Yeah. Nobody notices. Only if is wrong.
B: Ha, yes! Only if it's wrong. Are you near Basingstoke as well, then?
A: Yeah, Brighton Hill. You?
B: Didcot. So the other end of the A34, sort of.
A: The A34 is terrible.
B: Oh, it's awful. Every time I go to Newbury for fabric I sit there going, why do I do this.
A: Ha. Yeah.
B: Erm, have you got family? Sorry, I saw the drawing on your fridge, I'm being nosy.
A: Is fine. My son Oliver, he's ten. And my wife Claire. She puts everything on the fridge.
B: That's so funny, my fridge is exactly the same. I've got Isla, she's eight, and my husband Rob. I keep meeting people with my husband's name today.
A: Ha, me too. There is Claire in our group, and Rob.
B: Oh my gosh, yeah! It's like they planned it. Erm, do you make things at home too, or are you sick of wood by the weekend?
A: Er, I make things, but I don't finish. There is garden bench, nearly done for one year. Claire says, when is bench. I say, soon.
B: Oh, that's the same as Rob's shed! He's an electrician and he's been building a shed since about March. Half a roof.
A: Half roof is okay. Is like my bench, it has three legs.
B: Ha! Three legs is a start. I'd do you a cushion for it when it's finished.
A: Okay, deal. Then I have to finish it.
B: That's the plan, yeah. Do you ever do bespoke stuff, or just kitchens?
A: Just kitchens for the company. I think sometimes about my own business, wardrobes, alcoves, that kind of thing. There is good money. But the paperwork, the invoices, chasing people... I'm not good with that. I forget to take photos even for the Instagram.
